chunks: And from him, from al-Qasim, from Aban, from Abi al-'Abbas al-Fadl al-Baqbaq, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said concerning a well into which a mouse, or a beast, or a dog, or a bird falls and dies: It is taken out, then buckets are drawn from the well, then one may drink from it and perform wudu (ablution) with it.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةُ: a mouse falling into the well
key_terms.الْكَلْبُ: a dog falling into the well
key_terms.يَمُوتُ: dies in the well, causing the legal question
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: wudu (ablution) is performed with the water
key_terms.يُخْرَجُ: it is removed from the well
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: water is drawn out from the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on well water if a mouse, dog, or bird falls into it and dies?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a well in which an animal falls and dies. It states that after the carcass is removed and some buckets of water are drawn out, the water may be used for drinking and for wudu (ablution).
